summary: A first-person, PS1-style Mars survival game that lets students run an outpost for 7 sols. They balance power, oxygen, water, food and radiation shielding, then learn the real NASA science behind every crisis
details:
THE PROBLEM

Space STEM content often hides the engineering trade-offs that decide whether a mission succeeds, or makes them too complex for young learners.

OUR SOLUTION

Mars Outpost: Last Shift is a free browser game. The player is the new commander of Outpost Helios: the previous commander has collapsed and rescue lands in 7 sols. From a friendly command terminal the player manages five resources (Battery, Oxygen, Water, Food, Shield), shares limited power between life support, greenhouse, heating and communications, and spends a few action points each sol. Dust storms, solar particle events and equipment faults force real trade-offs, such as saving power or pushing on, sheltering or keeping working, recycling or rationing water.

HOW IT TEACHES

Each crisis ends with a "What NASA knows" debrief card that links the decision to a real example: the 2018 dust storm that silenced the Opportunity rover, astronauts sheltering during solar particle events, the space station recovering about 98% of its water, and Curiosity's radiation measurements. A hints assistant (HELIOS), a glossary, subtitles for all announcements, a large-text option and a reduce-flicker option help young players.

EXPLORATION

Players can also stand up, walk the outpost, put on a suit, cycle the airlock and step onto the Martian surface. The airlock refuses to open during flares and storms, which teaches why shielding and timing matter.

HONEST NUMBERS

Resource values are simplified game units, not real mission quantities. A Sources screen shows each constant as REAL, ADAPTED or GAME, with the source of the real facts.

BUILT WITH

Unity (WebGL), a custom simulation written separately from the interface so it can be tested, and a PS1-style low-poly look. It runs in any desktop browser at no cost. Built during the 2026 hackathon.
